batchName: Middle Republic: The Gracchi (133-121 BCE) - Medium Batch 1

questions.question: Why did the Roman consul at Numantia send Tiberius Gracchus to negotiate with the enemy?
options: The Numantines trusted his father's name
He spoke the local Celtiberian language
The Senate had named him as envoy
He was the most senior officer present
He had once been a hostage in Numantia
questions.explanation: Tiberius's father had governed the region decades earlier, so the Numantines trusted the family. Tiberius managed to save the trapped army.
questions.sourceQuote: The commanding consul sent Tiberius to negotiate, because the Numantines trusted his family name: his father had governed the region decades earlier.

questions.question: How did Tiberius deal with the fellow tribune who vetoed his land bill?
options: He prosecuted him for treason
He waited for his term to expire
He bribed him to withdraw the veto
He had him removed and voted out of office
He asked the Senate to exile him
questions.explanation: Deposing a tribune was unprecedented and unconstitutional. With the veto gone, the bill passed.
questions.sourceQuote: Tiberius had him physically removed and voted out of office, something without precedent and against the constitution.

questions.question: Where did Gaius Gracchus and his ally make their armed stand in 121 BC?
options: The temple of Castor in the Forum
A villa on the Palatine Hill
The temple of Diana on the Aventine
The fortifications on the Janiculum
The chief temple on the Capitoline
questions.explanation: Gaius and his ally armed their followers and occupied the Aventine temple. Opimius attacked with armed citizens and Cretan archers.
questions.sourceQuote: Gaius and his close ally armed their followers and seized the temple of Diana on the Aventine Hill, in the south of Rome.

questions.question: What prompted a senator to accuse Tiberius Gracchus of wanting to make himself king?
options: His raising of a private army
His plan to use the Pergamene bequest
His plan to marry an Egyptian princess
A crown offered to him by the crowd
His wearing of a purple royal robe
questions.explanation: By claiming the Pergamene windfall, Tiberius intruded on finance and foreign affairs, which belonged to the Senate.
questions.sourceQuote: Finance and foreign affairs belonged to the Senate, and a senator accused Tiberius of wanting to make himself king.

questions.question: What did Gaius Gracchus achieve as quaestor in Sardinia during a harsh winter?
options: He built a new harbour for the fleet
He collected years of unpaid taxes
He put down a slave uprising
He founded a Roman colony there
He got supplies from the islanders for the troops
questions.explanation: Gaius obtained supplies for the struggling Roman troops. When his commander's posting was extended, he went home without permission.
questions.sourceQuote: During a harsh winter he managed to obtain supplies from the islanders for the struggling Roman troops.

questions.question: Besides saving the Roman army, what did Tiberius persuade the Numantines to hand back?
options: The army's lost standards
Prisoners from an earlier war
His father's old sword
The captured Roman consul
His captured account books
questions.explanation: As quaestor, Tiberius kept the army's accounts, and he even recovered his captured books. Rome nonetheless rejected his treaty as humiliating.
questions.sourceQuote: Tiberius saved the army, and even persuaded the enemy to hand back his captured account books.

questions.question: What violent incident during a sacrifice in 121 BC set off the final crisis for Gaius Gracchus?
options: Gaius's house was set on fire
The consul Opimius was wounded by a dagger
An attendant was stabbed to death with styluses
A tribune was thrown from the Tarpeian Rock
A priest was murdered at the altar
questions.explanation: An attendant who jeered at the Gracchans was killed with writing styluses. Opimius then called the Senate together.
questions.sourceQuote: During a sacrifice, an attendant jeered at the Gracchans and was stabbed to death with writing styluses.

questions.question: Roughly how much public land did the old law Tiberius wanted to enforce allow one person to hold?
options: About 50 hectares (125 acres)
About 1,200 hectares (3,000 acres)
About 120 hectares (300 acres)
About 500 hectares (1,250 acres)
About 12 hectares (30 acres)
questions.explanation: Tiberius believed this old, widely ignored limit applied. His law would enforce it and give the surplus to poor citizens.
questions.sourceQuote: Tiberius believed that an old, widely ignored law limited how much public land anyone could hold to about 120 hectares (300 acres).

questions.question: Italian anger over the land commission helped lead to which later conflict?
options: The Jugurthine War
The Social War
The Servile War
The Numantine War
The Third Punic War
questions.explanation: The Social War was a later revolt of Rome's Italian allies. Some of their grievances began with land taken by the Gracchan commission.
questions.sourceQuote: Italian anger over the land helped lead to the Social War, a later revolt of the allies against Rome.

questions.question: How did the consul respond when Scipio Nasica demanded force to stop Tiberius's re-election?
options: He ordered troops to the Capitoline
He arrested Tiberius
He refused
He named a dictator
He fled the city
questions.explanation: After the consul refused, Nasica shouted the old emergency formula for raising troops and led the mob himself.
questions.sourceQuote: When the consul refused, Scipio Nasica shouted the old formula for raising troops in an emergency: "Let those who want the state to be safe follow me."
